chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: The first Hot Club of France concert at La Boite a Musique
summary: The first concert was given in a record shop basement by Johnson, Taylor, du Conge and Briggs, who were assigned low member numbers and played for nothing; the club later bought a house at 14 Rue Chaptal.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, he organized a concert, a first concert on the Boulevard Raspail in an establishment called the Music
Briggs 293
Box, La Boite a Musique, which was owned by Armand Bernard, who was a personal friend of mine; he deceased about ten years ago.
He was a Frenchman then?
A Frenchman, yes. He was the owner of that establishment, where we gave our first concert.
The first concert was given by Freddie Johnson, Billy Taylor, Pete du Conge, and Arthur Briggs. We were just four. That was the first concert given by what became the Hot Club of France.
And this little place was kind of a record store.
It was a record store.
Sheet music --
Yes, yes.
That kind of thing?
Briggs
Yeh. And Victrolas. Selling Victrolas.
Right, and it was down in the basement?
In the basement, yes.
Yeh, I see.
First floor and the basement. The basement and the first.
What kinds of tunes did you -- I mean it was a jazz band, I mean you were just there --
Just improvising.
Yeh.
Just improvising. It was -- you see there was four of us from Bricktop's.
Right.
And then we -- the Hot Club of France was formed, and he was member number 1, I was member number 2, or number 3, between Freddie Johnson and I,
Briggs
2 or 3, and Pete du Conge was 4, and Billy Taylor 5.
It was just one of those things. They just used us and gave us those numbers, original numbers, so they can have us work for nothing.
We realized it didn't mean anything, 'cause we just loved our profession, you see.
So, you were willing to come down and play these --
Oh, yes, we played all these, we played all the concerts, giving them enough money to buy the establishment that they had, 14 Rue Pigalle -- 14 Rue Chaptalle. 14 Rue Chaptalle.
Right.
They had a home -- they bought a home, a private home with the (unintelligible) formed into the Hot Club of France.
Well you -- this was then what, 193--
Briggs
As late as that?
Oh, yes. '34, yes. This all happened at the same time, when Panassie went -- I just mentioned his name -- it must be my age (Laughter).
Not Panassie?
No, just a second. Canetti. This all happened at the same time that Canetti was arranging for us to record and everything, you see, it all happened, at the same time.
